claims.claim: Developer trust in AI accuracy has collapsed from ~40% (2023-2024) to 29-33% (2025-2026), creating a well-documented 'adoption-trust paradox' where usage rises as confidence falls.

sources.name: Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2025
sources.contribution: Trust fell to 29%, 46% actively distrust, only 3% 'highly trust'

sources.name: Stack Overflow Blog: Closing the AI Trust Gap
sources.contribution: 11-percentage-point trust drop analysis, competence-confidence gap

sources.name: SonarSource State of Code Developer Survey 2026
sources.contribution: 96% don't fully trust AI code, only 48% always verify, 38% say review takes MORE effort

sources.name: Safeguard AI Trust Report 2026
sources.contribution: 34% trust code security, 21% trust dependency handling, 58% encountered unverifiable packages

contradictions.description: Perception vs reality of productivity: Developers feel 20% faster with AI, but RCTs show 19% slower for experienced devs. This 40-point gap is the central tension in the field.
contradictions.resolution: The gap is explained by 'vibes-based evaluation' — code looks right but fails in the 'last mile' (deprecated APIs, subtle bugs, hallucinated params). Seniors who verify rigorously slow down; juniors who don't verify feel faster but accumulate debt.

contradictions.description: Adoption rises (84%) while trust falls (29%) — counterintuitive correlation.
contradictions.resolution: Adoption is driven by competitive pressure and visible productivity signals, while trust falls because increased usage exposes more failure modes. Trust is not a prerequisite for adoption in this market.

deduplication_note: Multiple sources converged on same figures (84% adoption, 29% trust, 19% slower) — deduplicated to strongest primary source per claim
confidence_assessment: High confidence (0.89) — exceeds routing threshold of 0.85. Claims backed by large-n surveys, RCTs, and convergent multi-source evidence. Senior developer angle well-covered by Stack Overflow segmentation and qualitative analysis.
